Technology stocks were firming in recent trading following Monday's steep losses. At last look, shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 were adding more than 0.8% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was rising nearly 2.2%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) GDS Holdings ( GDS ) was 13% higher Tuesday afternoon after the Chinese data-center company reported an increase in Q3 revenue to RMB762.8 million from RMB424.4 million in same quarter last year and also raised its outlook for FY18 revenue. That beat the two-analyst mean of RMB706.8 million. Looking forward, the company also is expecting at least RMB2.75 billion in revenue for the 12 months ending Dec. 31. The upbeat revenue total and outlook have been helping GDS Holdings overcome below-consensus adjusted net income, posting a net loss of RMB0.96, or about $0.14, per American depositary share compared with RMB0.95 per ADS last year and missing the analyst consensus of RMB0.86 per ADS.
In other sector news:
(+) Magic Software Enterprises ( MGIC ) still was almost 1% higher Tuesday afternoon, falling off a nearly 4% gain earlier in the session that followed the Israeli software firm reporting improved adjusted Q3 net income and revenue compared with year-ago levels. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $0.14 per share during the September quarter compared with $0.12 per share during the same period a year ago. Total revenue rose year over year to $72.1 million from $65.7 million last year. Three analysts polled by Capital IQ had been expecting adjusted per-share net earnings of $0.15 on $73.4 million in revenue.
(-) EverQuote: plunged to a record low on Tuesday, sinking over 43% to a worst-ever $6.77 a share. On Monday the company reported a Q3 net loss wider than a year-ago despite an increase in revenue during the September quarter. Net loss for the three months ended Sept. 30 expanded to $0.15 per share, more than doubling the company's $0.07 per share net loss during the same quarter last year. Revenue rose to $41.7 million during the quarter, climbing 30% from $32.1 million last year. Analyst estimates were not available for comparison.
